- **Task:** Triage #3270: github-backup daily fetch — a missing mirror never reaches the chronic-failure exit code
- **Expectation:** effort/s — triage confirms the missing path (fetch_mirrors.py:22-23 returns before any fail_days record; chronic check at :72-75) against infra/github-backup/bin on main, then routes the fix (record missing days in state so repeated misses exit non-zero, clearing on the next ok)
- **Links:** https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3270
<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=new-issue-creator-code-a state=filed at=2026-11-01T00:48:18Z -->

🤖 Design-architect pass 29 (2026-10-31) — agent note: this issue is ADOPTED as a phase of design #3282 ("a mirror is what it can prove — one validity, outcome and alarm contract for the github-backup estate mirror", design doc: files/designs/code-github-backup-mirror-contract.md in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace), linked as a sub-issue of #3282 and labelled source/design-architect. Triage: do NOT re-file, re-scope or split this issue — record the phase structure instead. Phase mapping: Phase 1 (validity & destinations) = #3238 + #3233; Phase 2 (recorded outcomes & the alarm) = #3250 + #3219 + #3270 + #3257; Phase 3 (durable state & plan retention) = #3240 + #3229 + closing audit #3283 (gated on Phases 1–2). The design records the pins that span the phases: validity = bare + HEAD resolves, with no emptiness exception inside the plan (build_plan excludes zero-commit repos); destinations are absent / valid / skeleton (remove + clone) / debris (quarantine to `.partial-<timestamp>` + clone); every fetch attempt ends in one recorded outcome shared by the daily loop and the drainer, and the drainer acks only on `ok`; the chronic alarm is a streak of 3 consecutive unavailable days (fail, timeout and missing all count); generated state is written atomically only through `ghb_common` helpers; reconcile retains a failed owner's previously planned entries. Where an origin's acceptance left a choice open (the streak-vs-window rule, missing-counts-vs-immediate, report-vs-retain, skeleton handling), the design doc records the decision — triage follows the design's pin, not the open alternative. Each origin keeps its own acceptance criteria and its already-queued triage packet — no new packet was created for it this pass.

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=openchamber-scheduled-lane state=picked-up at=2026-11-01T15:00:51Z task=4781 -->

## Triage findings (task 4781)

Confirmed on current `main` (`5828cb8d71914ece6dc2c18836ef104e0e50c2a7`): `infra/github-backup/bin/fetch_mirrors.py:23-24` returns `missing` before state initialization at `:34`; the chronic check at `:80-82` counts only `fail_days`. A targeted isolated probe reproduced this: `fetch_repo` returned `missing`, left state `{}`, and the chronic condition stayed false. The pre-existing laptop probe recorded in this issue additionally showed three successive missing-only passes exiting 0.

**Route / decision:** this issue is already adopted into Phase 2 of design #3282, alongside #3250, #3219 and #3257; no duplicate issue or PR is needed. Follow the design pin: `missing` counts as an unavailable calendar day, the alarm is a streak of three consecutive unavailable days, and a later `ok` clears the record. This settles the immediate-vs-three-day choice in the existing acceptance criteria. No implementation was performed in this triage task.

- **Outcome:** confirmed on current main; routed to Phase 2 of #3282 under its pinned three-day streak decision. No new follow-up issue/PR.
- **Links:** https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3270 · https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3282
